name: Camunic
world_status: accessible description is silent on stress

earlier_scan.source_named: Camunic is an extinct fragmentarily attested inscription language; no stress description exists to find

sources.citation: Zavaroni, Adolfo. 2005-2009. 'Iscrizioni camune' archive index (Corpus Inscriptionum Camunnarum per site: Foppe di Nadro, Verdi, Zurla, Dos dell'Arca, Vite, Luine, Pia' d'Ort, Piancogno), simbolisullaroccia.it, Wayback 2011 snapshot.
sources.note: Index page only; the linked corpus PDFs are not archived (Wayback availability empty; Internet Archive partly offline at fetch time).

sources.citation: Marchesini, Simona. 2011. Alla ricerca del modello perduto. Sulla genesi dell'alfabeto camuno. Palaeohispanica 11: 155-171.
sources.note: Nothing on accent. On the alphabet's genesis; p.161: 'In mancanza di dati completi e aggiornati sull'epigrafia camuna, è difficile trarre ad oggi delle riflessioni sistematiche e strutturate sull'intera serie alfabetica e sull'effettivo funzionamento dei fonemi.' Corpus ca. 280 mostly very short rock inscriptions (p.156).

sources.citation: Zavaroni, Adolfo. 2004. Le iscrizioni camune. Centro Camuno di Studi Preistorici, Dipartimento Valcamonica e Lombardia (web article, 5 pp.; sections '1. Fonologia', 'Morfologia'). Wayback copy of http://www.simbolisullaroccia.it/PDF/ISCRIZIONI 2007 snapshot).
sources.note: Nothing. The 'Fonologia' section (pp.1-3) treats only letter values inferred from alphabetaria and inscriptions: absence of voiced stops, aspirates [h ph th], sibilant graphemes, 4+ vowel signs with possible o/u and length distinctions. No mention of accent/stress.

sources.citation: Mnamon. Antiche scritture del Mediterraneo (Scuola Normale Superiore, Pisa): alphabetical script index and 'Retico' page (Scrittura id=63).
sources.note: Mnamon has no Camunic entry at all (index checked); the Raetic page only mentions the arrow sign 'presente questo anche nel vicino alfabeto camuno'. Nothing on accent.

sources.citation: Schumacher, Stefan; Salomon, Corinna; Kluge, Sindy et al. Thesaurus Inscriptionum Raeticarum (University of Vienna, online), page 'Script', section 'Camunic'.
sources.note: Nothing. States: 'The language written in the rock inscriptions, called "Camunic" after the demonym Camunni documented by the ancients, has not yet been deciphered or convincingly connected to any of the surrounding languages'; main problem is even the identification of the letters.

sources.citation: Thesaurus Inscriptionum Raeticarum (University of Vienna, online), page 'Raetica'.
sources.note: Nothing; '(The linguistic affiliation of Camunic remains obscure.)'

sources.citation: Wikipedia EN 'Camunic language' and IT 'Lingua camuna' (used for bibliography leads and transliteration tables only).
sources.note: Nothing on accent; ~170 inscriptions, mostly a few words; 'The amount of material is insufficient to fully decipher the language.'
